definitions.explanation: Thin, thread-like structures found in plants, animals, or synthetic materials. Used in biology, nutrition, and materials science.
Fibers used as raw materials for textiles and fabrics. Also refers to the textile industry itself.

examples.japanese: {食物|しょくもつ}{繊維|せんい}を{多|おお}くとる。
examples.english: Get a lot of dietary fiber.

examples.japanese: {筋|きん}{繊維|せんい}が{傷|きず}ついている。
{野菜|やさい}には{食物|しょくもつ}{繊維|せんい}が{豊富|ほうふ}に{含|ふく}まれている。
examples.english: Vegetables are rich in dietary fiber.

examples.japanese: {化学|かがく}{繊維|せんい}のシャツは{乾|かわ}きやすい。
この{地域|ちいき}は{繊維|せんい}{産業|さんぎょう}で{栄|さか}えた。
examples.english: This region prospered from the textile industry.

examples.japanese: {天然|てんねん}{繊維|せんい}と{合成|ごうせい}{繊維|せんい}にはそれぞれ{長所|ちょうしょ}と{短所|たんしょ}がある。
examples.english: Natural fibers and synthetic fibers each have their strengths and weaknesses.

notes:
USAGE:
Very common in health and nutrition contexts as {食物|しょくもつ}{繊維|せんい} (dietary fiber). Also common in industry and materials contexts for textiles and fabrics.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {食物|しょくもつ}{繊維|せんい}: dietary fiber
- {化学|かがく}{繊維|せんい}: synthetic fiber
- {天然|てんねん}{繊維|せんい}: natural fiber
- {繊維|せんい}{産業|さんぎょう}: textile industry
- {繊維|せんい}{質|しつ}: fibrous, fiber content
- {筋|きん}{繊維|せんい}: muscle fiber
